arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Perkell argued Congress intended to require inmates to comply with administrative grievance procedures.
Mr. Feder argued a procedural default rule should not be read into the PLRA.
Mr. Himmelfarb argued the Ninth Circuit decision contradicts the text, history, and purposes of the PLRA.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests the scope of the Prison Litigation Reform Act. the sides that brought the case argue the law mandates using prison grievance procedures. the opposing sides claim the law allows inmates to skip those steps. The United States supports the sides that brought the case. The core conflict involves statutory interpretation and procedural requirements.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the procedural path for inmate lawsuits. It determines whether prisoners must navigate internal prison systems first. The outcome shapes access to federal courts for incarcerated individuals. It clarifies the balance between prison administration and judicial review.
